For $n\ge1$ and $D\ge0$, let $\mathcal F(n,D)$ be the set of $w:\{0,\dots,D\}\to[0,1]$ with $\sum w=n$, $w(0)>0$, $w(D)>0$, and $(w\star\tilde w)(d):=\sum_z w(z)w(z+d)\le1$ for every $d\ne0$. Every Sidon $A\subset[0,D]$ with $0,D\in A$ and $|A|=n$ has $1_A\in\mathcal F(n,D)$. Put $W(x)=\sum_{z\le x}w(z)$, $W'(x)=\sum_{z\ge D-x}w(z)$ and $x_j=2^{-j}D$, and define
$\Phi(w)=\sum_{j\ge1,\,x_j\ge n}(\lambda_j^{-2}+\lambda_j'^{-2})$ with $\lambda_j=nW(\lfloor x_j\rfloor)/x_j$ and $\lambda'_j$ defined likewise from $W'$. (This is the G1 functional; edge Cauchy–Schwarz gives $Q(A)\gtrsim\Phi(1_A)$.)
(a) Upper bound. Suppose $0<\delta\le1/2$, $\delta n^2\ge41$ and $n^2\ge3/\delta$, and set $D=\lfloor(1+\delta)n^2\rfloor$. Then some $w\in\mathcal F(n,D)$ has $\sum w^2\le1$ (so also $w\le1$, $w\star\tilde w\le1$ and $w*w\le1$ at every lag) and $\Phi(w)\le2(1+2\delta)^2(\log_2(1/\delta)+4.1)$.
(b) Lower bound. Suppose $n\ge16$, $3n^{-1/2}\le\delta\le1/2$ and $D\le(1+\delta)n^2$. Then every $w\in\mathcal F(n,D)$ has $\Phi(w)\ge(\log_2(1/\delta)-2)/18$.

Notation:
- w(x) = log log x / log x for x > 1.
- ω(m) is the number of distinct prime divisors of m.
- A positive integer is y-smooth if all its prime factors are ≤ y; 1 counts as smooth.
- E* = {n ∈ ℕ : ∃ k ∈ [0, 4000] with n+k 4000-smooth}.

Theorem.
(a) For every N ≥ 1, #(E* ∩ [0, N]) ≤ 4001·(1 + log(N+4000)/log 2)^{π(4000)}. Hence #(E* ∩ [0, N]) = (log N)^{O(1)}.
(b) For every n ∉ E* there is k ∈ [5, 2314] with ω(n+k) ≥ 6 and w(k) ≥ w(2314). Hence
  F(n) = max_k ω(n+k)·w(k) ≥ 6·w(2314) ≈ 1.585653 (to six decimals).

Conditional remark (not part of the theorem): the team's sharper constant 6w(2312) ≈ 1.585743 holds for all n ∉ E* if the CNF system of their step 4–5 is verified UNSAT for k0 = 3 and k0 = 4, for example by a checked DRAT/LRAT certificate.

- |E_n| ≤ 2/ρ(2/α') + o(1) = O_{θ,ε}(1).
- Let T₂(n) be the number of indices in [n/4, n/2] lying in e = 2 runs.
- Let T_{2,D}(n) be the number of those indices lying in kept pieces (defined in the proof) assigned to D, where F_D(x) = x² + x + (1−D)/4.

Then T₂(n) ≤ o(n) + Σ_{D∈E_n} T_{2,D}(n). Every D ∈ E_n with T_{2,D}(n) > 0 satisfies:

targets.statement: There is no distinct covering with moduli m = 3^a·s, where s is odd, square-free and coprime to 3, and a ≥ 0 is arbitrary.
Every distinct odd covering has a modulus divisible by 9.

There is an explicit P₀ (say ≤ 100) such that exponent-dependent distortion handles all primes p > P₀ with arbitrary exponents. Hence CORE follows from statement X: no distinct odd covering whose moduli are square-free outside the primes ≤ P₀. Prove the implication CORE ⇐ X.

No standard analytic conjecture (GRH, Hardy–Littlewood, abc, Hypothesis H) bears on this problem. For each M it is a finite combinatorial statement and no known conditional proof exists. New conditional target: assume the Prime-Power Distortion Hypothesis (PPDH). For every odd prime p and k ≥ 1, the BBMST stage inequality at p holds with loss factor ≤ 1 + 2/(p−1)², uniformly in k. Under PPDH, prov
Every distinct odd covering has ω(lcm) ≥ 10. Moreover, u(M) ≥ 1 for all odd M < 10^9.
There is no distinct odd covering in which every modulus has ω(m) ≤ 4.

Two parts. (a) The jinooklee "sieve monotonicity" is false. There exist odd M and M′ = M·p (with p | M) such that u(M′) < u(M). Concretely, compute u(45) < u(15) = 7 and u(3²·5·7) < u(3·5·7). (b) Every method that only certifies infeasibility of the LP relaxation fails for all odd abundant M, since uniform weights give a fractional cover.

Fix the ring F₂[x]. Show there is no covering of F₂[x] by residue classes with distinct monic moduli of positive degree that are all coprime to x(x+1). These moduli have no "norm-2" prime factor, the analogue of oddness. More generally, prove the same over F_q[x] with moduli free of linear factors.

In any distinct odd covering with lcm M, the classes at moduli 3^j·s with j = v₃(M) cannot all be removed. That is, every minimal odd covering uses the top 3-adic level. More strongly, v₃(M) ≤ C·log(ω(M)).
For square-free odd M, the uncovered density of any distinct cover is ≥ c₀·∏_{p|M}(1 − 1/p)^{α} with explicit c₀ > 0 and α < 1. Extend this to M with v₃(M) ≤ 2.
If A ⊂ [2,∞) is finite and pairwise coprime, then F(m)/m < 2F(n)/n for all m > n ≥ max A.
If A is primitive, n ≥ max A, and lcm(a,b,c) > n for all distinct a, b, c ∈ A ("depth 2 at scale n"), then F(m)/m < 2F(n)/n for all m > n.
There is an absolute C (target C ≤ 4) such that sup_{m>n} F(m)/m ≤ C·F(n)/n for every finite A ⊂ [2,∞) and every n ≥ max A. A first milestone is the m=∞ version, δ(A) ≤ C·F(n)/n.

Every inclusion-minimal counterexample (A, n, m) satisfies: - max A ≤ n/8; - for every a ∈ A, N_{C_a}(n/a) ≤ n/(4a), i.e. its private multiples at scale n are at most a quarter of its multiples; - some a has at least 3 elements of C_a below n/a.
Assume D₂: δ(A) < 2F_A(n)/n for every finite A ⊂ [2,∞) and every n ≥ max A. Prove that #488 follows, i.e. finite m reduces to m=∞, possibly by applying D₂ to auxiliary sets built from A and m.

In F_q[T], let A be a finite set of monic polynomials of degree ≥ 1, and let f(d) be the proportion of monic polynomials of degree d that are divisible by some element of A. Then f(m) < 2f(n) for all m > n ≥ max deg A. Also determine the optimal constant.
Construct primitive A and m > n with max A < 3n/14 and F(m)/m ≥ 1.4·F(n)/n. Alternatively, show that the supremum c* of the ratio in this regime is at least 1.3.

Let X be the statement: for every primitive A with |A| ≥ 2 and every m > n ≥ max A, some a ∈ A satisfies N_{C_a}(m/a)/m ≤ 2N_{C_a}(n/a)/n. Then X implies #488. Proof by induction on |A|, using the exact identity F_A = F_{A∖a} + N_{C_a}(·/a): - the singleton case holds because ⌊m/a⌋/m ≤ 1/a < 2⌊n/a⌋/n; - for |A| ≥ 2, F_A(m)/m = F_{A∖a}(m)/m + N_{C_a}(m/a)/m < 2F_{A∖a}(n)/n + 2N_{C_a}(n/a)/n. #488 holds for all A with |A| = 3.

μ_3 > √10. That is, exhibit a 3-sunflower-free "composable gadget" whose recursive composition gives f(n,3) > (3.17)^n.
There is an absolute C such that every 3-sunflower-free n-partite family with all blocks of size ≤ (log n)^{10} has size ≤ C^n.
SMC(2). There is an absolute κ_0 such that every κ_0-spread n-uniform family contains two disjoint members. Ideally κ_0 = 4 + o(1), matching iterated majority.
Let c(q) = lim_n (max sunflower-free code in [q]^n)^{1/n}. Prove c(q) = o(q), or even c(q) ≤ C q^{1−ε}.

There is a 2-connected graph with exactly two vertices of degree 2, all others of degree ≥ 3, and no cycle of length 2^k. Hence the conjecture fails in Bondy–Vince's "all but two vertices" setting, whereas the "all but one vertex" version is equivalent to the conjecture.

If every 2-connected graph with δ ≥ 3 contains C_{2^k}, then every graph with δ ≥ 3 does. By KNOWN this is equivalent to: given the 2-connected δ ≥ 3 case, every 2-connected graph with exactly one degree-2 vertex contains C_{2^k}.

Thickened (multiplicative-window) analogue: there is η > 0 such that every graph with δ ≥ 3 has a cycle whose length lies in ⋃_{k≥2} [2^k, (2−η)·2^k]. Stepping lemma: every 2-connected graph with δ ≥ 3 and girth g ∈ ((2−η)·2^k, 2^{k+1}) has a cycle of length in [2^{k+1}, (2−η)·2^{k+1}].
